text.name: rhm_help_overview_sub1
text.text: Power Balance: Machine Drag & Crop Threshing

text.name: rhm_help_overview_1
text.text: Realistic Harvesting completely replaces arcade fixed harvesting speeds with a physical engine power balance model based on ASABE and DLG standards. In vanilla gameplay, a combine always travels at maximum header speed regardless of crop density. In this mod, all available engine horsepower is dynamically divided among four real tasks: base drivetrain and hydrostatic drag (8% of rated power for grain combines, 10% for heavy root harvesters), mechanical header cutterbar and reel drive, the energy required to thresh and pull plant biomass through the cylinder or rotor, and additional resistance from crop moisture or weed infestation. The engine load percentage on your display indicates the exact share of available horsepower in use at any given second.

text.name: rhm_help_overview_2
text.text: You no longer need to constantly guess and adjust cruise control speed on the fly. Lower your header, engage the thresher, and enter the crop: the combine begins harvesting at a safe entry speed of 5.5 km/h, allowing crop material to evenly fill the feederhouse without shocking the threshing drum. From there, the intelligent hydrostatic controller automatically modulates ground speed to maintain engine load in its sweet spot (around 80–90%). If the machine encounters an unusually dense crop stand or climbs a steep hill, the system smoothly decelerates (0.45 s response time) to prevent drum slugging or engine stall. In lighter stands, it gently accelerates back up. Ground speed is always strictly capped by the factory header limit.

text.name: rhm_help_overview_3
text.text: Your straw management setting directly dictates how much horsepower remains for machine propulsion. The straw chopper is a high-inertia rotor spinning at over 3,000 RPM. Chopping and spreading straw demands 15% to 20% of total engine power, particularly in fibrous crops like oats, barley, or rye. If your combine is struggling to maintain forward speed under heavy load, switch straw processing to windrow/swath mode using the standard game control. The chopper rotor disengages, releasing dozens of horsepower back to the threshing mechanism and immediately boosting forward working speed by 1.5–3 km/h under identical engine load.

text.name: rhm_help_hud_1
text.text: When you board a combine, a sleek dark-glass telemetry capsule appears at the bottom of your screen. It features four primary indicators: Cell 1 displays engine load percentage with dynamic color coding (green up to 85% for comfortable operation; yellow from 85% to 95% indicating the optimal efficiency zone; red above 95% warning of overload). Cell 2 displays real-time grain loss percentage or recommended ground speed. Cell 3 shows current crop moisture percentage or field working pace in hectares per hour. Cell 4 presents instantaneous crop yield (t/ha or bu/ac) or total combine throughput (t/h or l/h).

text.name: rhm_help_hud_2
text.text: The telemetry HUD can be positioned anywhere on your monitor. Click and hold the Left Mouse Button (LMB) on the panel and drag it to your preferred position so it never obstructs your cabin visibility. Moving near screen borders or the bottom edge of the F1 help menu triggers magnetic snapping, locking the HUD cleanly into alignment. Furthermore, the panel is fully interactive: a single left-click on Cells 2, 3, or 4 instantly toggles alternate telemetry views (for example, switching from tons per hour to hectares per hour, or between grain loss percentage and suggested speed).

text.name: rhm_help_hud_sub3
text.text: Sensor Availability & Dashes (--%) on Older Machines

text.name: rhm_help_hud_3
text.text: If you board an entry-level or vintage harvester and see dashes (--%) instead of grain loss or crop moisture readings, this is realistic intended behavior rather than a bug. Entry-level combines (Tier 1) lack physical piezoelectric loss sensors and optical moisture meters; the operator must monitor engine tone and tank grain sample cleanliness. Sieve loss sensors become functional upon purchasing the Tier 2 electronics upgrade in the workshop, while digital moisture sensing unlocks with Tier 3 and above. When pausing for a grain trailer or lifting the header on headlands, the HUD latches the last stable yield reading, preventing erratic zero-flickering.

text.name: rhm_help_calibration_main_text
text.text: Press Right Shift + K inside the cabin to open the touch calibration terminal. Base combines (Tier 1) feature purely mechanical controls: profile save, load, and autopilot buttons are padlocked, and optimal guide bars are hidden. To tune a base machine: use the reset button at the bottom to return all controls to neutral 50%. Adjust sliders according to standard harvesting practices: for small grains (wheat, barley), set the drum to 60–70%, cleaning fan to 65–75%, and sieve clearances to 50–60%. For large, fragile seeds (corn, sunflower), drum speed must be reduced to 35–45% to prevent rasp bars from cracking grain into dockage.

text.name: rhm_help_calibration_rotor_sub
text.text: Calibrating Tier 2–3: Green Sweet-Spots & Profile Memory

text.name: rhm_help_calibration_rotor_text
text.text: Upgrading your combine to Tier 2 reveals bright green sweet-spot target zones on every slider, computed specifically for the crop in the feederhouse. First-time setup: harvest a few meters into the field so the combine detects crop type, open the terminal (Shift+K), and adjust each slider using the [-] and [+] buttons into the green zone. Immediately click 'SAVE'! The machine stores these parameters into its profile memory. Once saved, the 'LOAD' button becomes active: whenever you return to this crop later, clicking 'LOAD' instantly restores your custom tuning. On Tier 3 machines, dynamic cards for engine load, mechanical efficiency, and predicted loss appear.

text.name: rhm_help_calibration_presets_sub
text.text: One-Touch Automatic Calibration on Tier 4 Combines

text.name: rhm_help_calibration_presets_text
text.text: Owners of flagship combines equipped with the Tier 4 electronics package (Opti-Harvest AI) never need to adjust sliders or manage save files manually. An 'AI AUTO-CALIB' button unlocks in the top-right corner: a single touch reads crop moisture and stand density, configuring optimal threshing settings in one second directly from the factory agronomic database. Furthermore, active cruise autopilot automatically trims drum RPM and fan speed every 2 seconds on the go whenever you encounter weedy patches or damp lowlands.

text.name: rhm_help_presets_sub1
text.text: Universal Settings: Why RPM and mm are identical across all combines

text.name: rhm_help_presets_1
text.text: On the in-cab calibration tablet (Right Shift + K), all parameters are displayed in real physical units: revolutions per minute (RPM) and clearance gap (mm). Fundamental agronomic rule: base optimal settings for any crop are IDENTICAL across all combine models, regardless of engine power (from 300 to 800 hp) or header width! Biological properties of wheat ears or corn cobs do not change: wheat always requires cylinder peripheral speed around ~800 RPM and air flow around ~960 RPM, otherwise grain remains unthreshed or is blown out with chaff. Engine horsepower and header width determine only working speed (km/h) and throughput (t/h), which the RHM system regulates automatically to prevent overload.

text.name: rhm_help_presets_2
text.text:
For entry-level harvesters (Tier 1) without sweet-spot illumination, use these factory baseline values:
- Wheat: Rotor Speed 780–820 RPM | Concave Clearance 5–7 mm | Fan Speed 940–980 RPM | Upper Sieve 14–15 mm | Lower Sieve 6–8 mm.
- Barley: Rotor 780–820 RPM | Concave 6–8 mm | Fan 980–1020 RPM | Upper Sieve 14–15 mm | Lower Sieve 7–9 mm (tough awns require aggressive separation air).
- Oat: Rotor 680–720 RPM | Concave 5–7 mm | Fan 730–770 RPM | Upper Sieve 14–16 mm | Lower Sieve 6–8 mm (light hulls; fan >850 RPM blows grain out).
- Corn (Maize): Rotor 310–350 RPM | Concave 28–32 mm | Fan 930–970 RPM | Upper Sieve 19–21 mm | Lower Sieve 11–13 mm (CAUTION: minimum rotor speed to avoid cob shattering!).
- Sunflower: Rotor 340–380 RPM | Concave 23–27 mm | Fan 730–770 RPM | Upper Sieve 17–19 mm | Lower Sieve 9–11 mm (gentle threshing protects brittle heads).
- Canola (Rapeseed): Rotor 480–520 RPM | Concave 16–19 mm | Fan 680–720 RPM | Upper Sieve 8–10 mm | Lower Sieve 3–5 mm (fine seeds; fan >750 RPM blows crop out).
- Soybean: Rotor 540–580 RPM | Concave 17–19 mm | Fan 960–1000 RPM | Upper Sieve 15–17 mm | Lower Sieve 8–10 mm (moderate rotor protects delicate embryos).
- Peas, Beans, Pulses: Rotor 410–450 RPM | Concave 14–16 mm | Fan 980–1020 RPM | Upper Sieve 17–19 mm | Lower Sieve 8–10 mm.
- Rice & Long Grain Rice: Rotor 700–740 RPM | Concave 6–8 mm | Fan 1030–1070 RPM | Upper Sieve 15–17 mm | Lower Sieve 6–8 mm (abrasive damp straw).
- Sorghum: Rotor Speed 580–620 RPM | Concave Clearance 17–19 mm | Fan Speed 1080–1120 RPM | Upper Sieve 14–16 mm | Lower Sieve 7–8 mm (dense seedheads require high airflow to clear heavy chaff).
- Grass Seed (Poppy, Clover): Rotor 780–820 RPM | Concave 4–6 mm | Fan 430–470 RPM | Upper Sieve 6–8 mm | Lower Sieve 2–4 mm (minimum airflow!).

text.name: rhm_help_presets_sub3
text.text: Forage, Root Crops, and Specialized Harvesters

text.name: rhm_help_presets_3
text.text:
For specialized machinery, Shift+K activates respective machine units:
- Forage Harvesters: Grain losses are zero (0%). Corn silage — Blower Speed 1300–1350 RPM, Chopping Drum 1150–1170 RPM, Feed Rolls 470–500 RPM. Swath pickup (hay/straw) — Blower 1150–1200 RPM, Drum 1070–1100 RPM, Feed Rolls 450–470 RPM. Direct grass cut — Blower 1230–1270 RPM, Drum 1120–1140 RPM, Feed Rolls 410–430 RPM. Poplar (woodchips) — Blower 1350–1400 RPM, Chopping Drum 1180–1200 RPM, Feed Rolls 380–400 RPM.
- Root Harvesters: Potato — Separation Blower 600–620 RPM, Cleaning Rollers 190–210 RPM, Elevator Web 300–320 RPM (cushions tubers against bruising). Sugar Beet, Beetroot (Red Beet) — Blower 630–650 RPM, Rollers 230–250 RPM, Elevator Web 290–310 RPM. Carrots, Parsnips — Blower 620–640 RPM, Rollers 200–220 RPM, Elevator Web 300–310 RPM. Onions — Blower 840–860 RPM, Rollers 200–220 RPM, Elevator Web 260–270 RPM.
- Vegetables: Green Beans — Cleaning Blower 700–720 RPM, Stripper Drum 170–190 RPM, Elevator Web 280–300 RPM. Spinach — Blower 550–580 RPM, Cutting Reel 140–160 RPM, Elevator Web 270–290 RPM (gentle leaf intake).
- Cotton: Blower Fan 3600–3800 RPM, Picker Speed (Spindles) 210–230 RPM, Feeder Drums 210–230 RPM.
- Sugar Cane: Primary Extractor Fan 1150–1200 RPM, Billet Chopper Drums 180–200 RPM, Elevator Conveyor 280–300 RPM.
- Grapes: Shaker Speed 450–470 RPM, Conveyor Speed 110–120 RPM, Extractor Fans 1250–1300 RPM.
- Olives: Beater Speed 540–560 RPM, Conveyor Speed 105–115 RPM, Extractor Fans 1300–1350 RPM.

text.name: rhm_help_presets_sub4
text.text: Crop Moisture: Physical Effects and Live Calibration Offsets

text.name: rhm_help_presets_4
text.text:
RHM supports external moisture mods (mapping live field wetness) and includes an internal diurnal weather simulator (16–18% morning dew, 11–13.5% dry afternoon golden window, >22% rain). Safe moisture threshold is 14.0% (canola: 9.0%). Each 1% moisture above limit adds +2% engine power drag and +0.35% unavoidable grain loss as damp kernels adhere to wet straw.
Calibration rule when moisture exceeds 14%:
1. Add +50...80 RPM to rotor speed (e.g. 860 RPM instead of 800 RPM for wheat) — relieves drag by pulling wet straw through the cylinder.
2. Add +30...50 RPM to fan speed (990 RPM instead of 950 RPM) — lifts heavy wet chaff off the shoe.
3. Open upper sieve +1...2 mm wider.
On Tier 2–3 harvesters, the green sweet-spot automatically shifts higher; on Tier 4 Opti-Harvest AI auto-trims settings continuously.

text.name: rhm_help_presets_sub5
text.text: Modded Crops and Custom Maps: Integrated Presets & Auto-Discovery

text.name: rhm_help_presets_5
text.text:
1. Supported Mod Crops in RHM Database:
- Rye, Triticale, Spelt: adjust as wheat (Rotor 780–820 RPM, Concave 5–7 mm, Fan 940–980 RPM, Sieves 14/7 mm).
- Buckwheat: Rotor 530–570 RPM, Concave 12–14 mm, Fan 730–770 RPM, Sieves 12/6 mm (fragile hulls).
- Millet: Rotor 780–820 RPM, Concave 5–7 mm, Fan 850–890 RPM, Sieves 14/7 mm.
- Flax/Linseed, Mustard: Rotor 830–870 RPM, Concave 14–16 mm, Fan 780–820 RPM, Sieves 9/4 mm.
- Poppy: Rotor 430–470 RPM, Concave 12–14 mm, Fan 430–470 RPM, Sieves 7/3 mm (micro seeds!).
- Hemp: Rotor 630–670 RPM, Concave 12–14 mm, Fan 830–870 RPM, Sieves 14/7 mm.
- Safflower: adjust as sunflower (Rotor 340–380 RPM, Fan 730–770 RPM, Sieves 18/10 mm).
- Clover / Grass Seed: Rotor 780–820 RPM, Concave 4–6 mm, Fan 430–470 RPM, Sieves 7/3 mm.
- Alfalfa (Forage): Silage — Blower ~1250, Drum ~1130, Feed Rolls ~420 RPM.
2. Auto-Discovery Engine for Custom Map Crops: RHM parses seed liter mass and straw presence directly from the map. 4-Family Rule for Tier 1: cereals with straw — tune as wheat; small oilseeds — tune as canola; large pulses — tune as peas/beans; tiny grasses — minimum air. On Tier 2–4, green sweet-spots calculate automatically.

text.name: rhm_help_trip_sub1
text.text: Current Field Logbook: Precision Harvest Accounting

text.name: rhm_help_trip_1
text.text: Press Right Shift + J inside the cabin to open the comprehensive four-tab analytical hub. The first tab is a digital field job odometer providing rigorous operational telemetry: it tallies harvested area in hectares, measures total harvested grain weight in metric tons and liters, records net harvesting time (excluding unloading halts and headland turns), and calculates average field yield along with real working productivity in tons and hectares per hour. You always know true field output long before hauling grain to the elevator.

text.name: rhm_help_trip_sub2
text.text: Financial Crop Loss, Driver Score & Cause Diagnostics

text.name: rhm_help_trip_2
text.text: The odometer not only logs lost grain tonnage, but also calculates financial revenue loss in game currency (€, $, or £) based on current crop market prices. A specialized agronomic scoring algorithm grades operator performance from [A] (exemplary driving, loss below 1%) down to [E] (poor driving, high losses). Beneath the letter grade, four diagnostic bars break down exact loss sources: excessive forward speed, crop moisture, sickle bar wear, or cross-slope chassis tilt on hillsides.

text.name: rhm_help_trip_sub3
text.text: Quick In-Cab Odometer Reset (Right Shift + R)

text.name: rhm_help_trip_3
text.text: When entering a new field or starting a benchmark run, you don't need to open menus: press and hold Right Shift + R for 1 second directly behind the steering wheel. The trip counter immediately resets to zero, accompanied by an audible chime and on-screen notification. Additionally, the game settings menu provides an automatic reset feature (Smart) that resets the odometer automatically whenever you cross into a new field number or switch crops in the grain tank.

text.name: rhm_help_trip_sub4
text.text: Field Registry, Seasonal Records & Fleet Monitoring

text.name: rhm_help_trip_4
text.text: The 'Farm Fields' tab tracks all owned parcels, preserving acreage and historical yields. The 'Season Analytics' tab charts monthly and yearly harvest trends. The 'Combine Fleet' tab allows farm managers to monitor all harvesting machinery in real time from anywhere: view active operators (player or hired worker), current crop, ground speed, engine load, throughput in tons per hour, cutterbar wear percentage, and installed electronics tier.

text.name: rhm_help_croploss_sub1
text.text: Physical Grain Deduction Directly from Grain Tank

text.name: rhm_help_croploss_1
text.text: In Realistic Harvesting, losses are not cosmetic visual effects. Grain that fails to separate or gets blown over the sieves with chaff is physically deducted in real time directly from the combine's grain tank! Driving too fast visibly reduces grain volume, causing 5% to 15% lower yields hauled to storage compared to clean harvesting. When windrowing straw, lost grain is deposited into the straw swath. On forage harvesters and cotton pickers, grain loss is disabled since biomass is harvested in its entirety.

text.name: rhm_help_croploss_sub2
text.text: Four Primary Loss Factors & How to Eliminate Them

text.name: rhm_help_croploss_2
text.text: Total crop losses stem from four distinct factors: 1. Speed & Overload: under ISO 8210 standards, separation losses start emerging above 80% engine load, exceed 1% allowable threshold at 95% load, and cause severe shoe drowning above 110% with grain spewing onto the ground. Keep engine load between 85–90%. 2. Moisture & Dew: crop moisture above 14% causes damp straw to mats together, adding +0.35% loss per 1% excess moisture. Harvest grains during sunny daylight hours. 3. Cutterbar Wear: dull sickle sections (above 15% wear) shatter seed heads before entering the feederhouse (up to 3% loss). Repair headers promptly in the workshop. 4. Field Slope: chassis tilt above 4° shifts grain to one side of the sieves, causing up to 5% loss.

text.name: rhm_help_croploss_3
text.text: When engine load exceeds 95% or real-time grain loss surpasses 5%, the in-cab terminal emits an authentic acoustic agricultural alert. In recommended Smart Buzzer mode, it sounds three discreet 0.3-second pulses followed by an 18-second grace period, keeping the operator alert without irritating continuous beeping. Hearing the alert is your signal to ease back ground speed, verify sieve settings in Shift+K, or switch off the straw chopper to immediately stem grain losses. Buzzer volume can be adjusted from 0% to 100% in game settings.

text.name: rhm_help_upgrades_sub1
text.text: Machinery Upgrades in Workshop: 4 Budgets & Tiers

text.name: rhm_help_upgrades_1
text.text: Any combine in the game (at initial dealership purchase or retrofitted in the farm workshop) can be equipped with an RHM electronics package. Park in the repair zone, press the configure key, and select 'RHM Electronics Package'. Four tiers are available: Tier 1 'Standard' (0 €, factory mechanical base), Tier 2 'Sensor Suite' (3,500 €), Tier 3 'Yield Monitor' (8,500 €), and Tier 4 'Opti-Harvest AI' (15,000 €). The active tier is displayed in the header of Shift+K and the fleet log.

text.name: rhm_help_upgrades_2
text.text: Tier 1 combines feature pure mechanical controls without sensors: the HUD displays dashes instead of loss readings, the calibration tablet lacks guidance aids, the driver relies on engine pitch, and hired AI workers make substantial calibration errors (up to ±18%). Tier 2 (3,500 €) is the primary starting upgrade for operators: it installs piezoelectric sieve loss sensors (live loss % on HUD) and unlocks bright green sweet-spot targets in Shift+K. Hired worker calibration error drops to ±10%.

text.name: rhm_help_upgrades_3
text.text: Tier 3 (8,500 €) adds an optical crop moisture sensor (moisture % on HUD), displays live engine load and efficiency telemetry in Shift+K, enables custom machine profile saving, and unlocks fleet monitoring in Shift+J (worker error drops to ±4%). Flagship Tier 4 (15,000 €) unlocks full autopilot capability: 'AI AUTO-CALIB' tunes the combine in one touch, dynamic trimming adjusts drum RPM and fan speed every 2 seconds to match field dampness, crop moisture penalty is reduced by 50%, and hired helpers harvest with 0% error.

text.name: rhm_help_ai_workers_1
text.text: Standard game AI helpers and automated workers no longer harvest at artificial full header speeds while dumping grain onto the ground. RHM enforces speed governance directly through the engine motor unit, keeping hired helpers strictly within a safe 85–95% load range. On rolling terrain or heavy stands, if harvest losses exceed your farm threshold (2.0%), the combine smoothly decelerates the worker automatically to safeguard grain yield from spilling into straw.

text.name: rhm_help_ai_workers_sub2
text.text: Worker Competence: Machine Tier Impact on Quality

text.name: rhm_help_ai_workers_2
text.text: When a hired worker takes the wheel, they calibrate combine operating parameters independently. The quality of their work directly reflects the combine's installed electronic package: on Tier 1 machines, workers operate like inexperienced trainees, miscalibrating settings by up to ±18% (causing elevated losses or fuel waste). On Tier 2, error decreases to ±10%; on Tier 3, error drops to ±4%; and on Tier 4 with Opti-Harvest, workers operate with 0% error, delivering showroom-grade harvest efficiency.

text.name: rhm_help_ai_workers_3
text.text: If you manually calibrate the combine in Shift+K or save a crop profile, check game settings: the 'AI Worker Settings' option defaults to 'Retain Mine'. In this mode, hired workers respect your precise tuning and never override it. 'Auto-Tune' lets helpers recalculate parameters based on machine tier, while 'Disabled' forbids helper adjustments entirely. On-the-go grain trailer unloading is fully supported without interrupting combine progress.

text.name: rhm_help_moisture_sub1
text.text: Diurnal Humidity Cycle: Selecting Optimal Field Hours

text.name: rhm_help_moisture_1
text.text: The mod computes an autonomous harmonic diurnal humidity cycle and interfaces with external weather systems when present. Crop vegetation moisture fluctuates predictably throughout the 24-hour cycle: between 03:00 and 08:00 AM, heavy dew raises grain moisture to 16–18% — harvesting is inadvisable due to heavy threshing resistance. From 08:00 to 11:30 AM, morning sun evaporates moisture. The golden harvesting window runs from 11:30 AM to 18:30 PM: solar heat dries crops to optimal 11–13%, straw becomes brittle, the combine glides smoothly, and losses drop to zero. After 19:30 PM, evening dew returns, increasing threshing drag.

text.name: rhm_help_moisture_sub2
text.text: Why Harvesting in Rain is Prohibited

text.name: rhm_help_moisture_2
text.text: During rain showers, crop moisture rapidly exceeds 22%. Soaked straw loses fluidity, forming dense tangled mats that plug feederhouses and blind cleaning sieves. Grain sticks to damp straw and is carried straight out the rear, generating up to 10% direct crop loss while the engine struggles under tripled mechanical resistance. Beginner advice: if rain begins, shut down the combine and wait out the weather. Harvesting in the rain only forfeits crop yield and farm revenue.

text.name: rhm_help_moisture_sub3
text.text: How to Tune Your Combine for Damp Crops (14–16%)

text.name: rhm_help_moisture_3
text.text: When damp crops (14–16%) must be harvested, never max out sliders blindly! Open the Shift+K tablet: elevated moisture automatically shifts the green sweet-spot target zones upward for both the drum and cleaning fan. Adjust sliders to stay strictly inside the shifted green band: higher drum speed within the green zone tears tough damp straw easily, while higher fan speed keeps heavy wet chaff airborne. Caution: cranking the fan too high into the red zone will blow clean grain right out onto the field, causing instant losses! Stay inside the green zone for 0% tuning loss. On Tier 4 machines, Opti-Harvest manages these adjustments automatically.

text.name: rhm_help_special_title
text.text: 10. Forage Harvesters, Root Crops & Special Machinery

text.name: rhm_help_special_sub1
text.text: Self-Propelled Forage Harvesters: Power Split & Windrows

text.name: rhm_help_special_1
text.text: Forage harvesters chop entire crop plants into silage, so grain loss is inherently zero (0%). Engine power demand is split between three distinct mechanisms: feed rolls (18%), chopping drum (62%), and discharge accelerator blower (20%). When gathering grass haylage or straw windrows with a pickup header, monitor windrow thickness: oversized or lumpy windrows bottleneck the feed rolls, creating sharp driveline resistance and slowing forward speed.

text.name: rhm_help_special_sub2
text.text: Root Crop Harvesters: Why Lifters Run at 5–8 km/h

text.name: rhm_help_special_2
text.text: Underground root crops (potatoes, sugar beets, carrots, parsnips, onions) demand enormous draft power: subterranean share blades slice dense soil beds, drawing 7 horsepower per meter of working width in addition to 10% base hydrostatic chassis drag. Consequently, self-propelled beet and potato harvesters cannot travel faster than 5–8 km/h even with engines rated over 600 HP. Top-harvested vegetables (green beans, peas, spinach) avoid soil lifting, but stripping reels draw substantial mechanical energy to pluck pods.

text.name: rhm_help_special_sub3
text.text: Cotton, Grapes, Olives & Modular Carriers (NEXAT / NEXCO)

text.name: rhm_help_special_3
text.text: Cotton harvesters draw up to 55 HP per ton of seed cotton to spin picking drums and hydraulically compress round modules. Grape and olive harvesters account for the power draw of vibrating shaker rods and suction cleaning fans. If you operate the wide-span 1,100 HP NEXAT system tractor paired with the NEXCO combine module, RHM automatically propagates carrier engine horsepower through attached implement hierarchies, guaranteeing seamless operation without power loss.

text.name: rhm_help_difficulty_sub1
text.text: Game Styles: Choosing Between Arcade, Moderate & Realistic

text.name: rhm_help_difficulty_1
text.text: If you prefer not to calculate horsepower or tune threshing drums, select a streamlined playstyle in the pause menu (Escape → Game Settings): Motor Difficulty set to 'Arcade' (Level 1) disables engine load physics and removes speed caps. Loss Difficulty set to 'Arcade' eliminates grain loss entirely, allowing combines to harvest at maximum header speed like vanilla. Level 2 ('Moderate') cushions errors, while Level 3 ('Realistic') engages full physical simulation with authentic grain tank deductions.

text.name: rhm_help_difficulty_sub2
text.text: Physics Feature Toggles: Tailoring Your Experience

text.name: rhm_help_difficulty_2
text.text: You don't need to disable all physics at once — toggle individual mechanics to suit your preferences: disable 'Wear Losses' if you prefer not to track sickle sharpness; disable 'Slope Losses' when farming mountainous terrain; disable 'Moisture Simulation' to harvest at night or in rain without penalties. The 'Power Boost' setting adds +5% to +50% reserve engine horsepower, ideal for challenging steep hillside maps.

text.name: rhm_help_difficulty_sub3
text.text: Audio Alerts, Measurement Units & Multiplayer Rules

text.name: rhm_help_difficulty_3
text.text: In audio settings, configure the overload alert to 'Smart Buzzer' (three gentle pulses), 'Continuous', or 'Disabled', and adjust the volume slider (0% to 100%) with instant audio test playback. Telemetry units can be toggled between Metric (t/ha, t/h), Imperial, and Bushels. In multiplayer, physics rules are governed exclusively by the server administrator, while HUD positioning, audio alerts, and display units are customized individually by each player.

text.name: rhm_msg_req_tier2
text.text: Profiles require Sensors Package (Tier 2 or higher)

text.name: rhm_msg_profile_not_found
text.text: No saved profile found for this crop

text.name: rhm_setting_ai_tuning_long
text.text: Controls how hired workers and Courseplay handle combine calibration. 'Keep Player Settings' strictly respects and retains your adjustments or loaded profiles. 'Always Auto-Tune' recalculates settings based on electronics tier. 'Disabled' prevents helpers from ever changing combine settings.

text.name: rhm_setting_enableTutorials_long
text.text: Show interactive onboarding hints and tips during harvesting.

text.name: rhm_tut_welcome_msg
text.text: Welcome to Realistic Harvesting! Combine speed is dynamically controlled by engine load, crop density, and width. Monitor your HUD and press (Right Shift + K) to open the Calibration Terminal.

text.name: rhm_tut_overload_msg
text.text: The engine is under extreme strain! The hydrostatic transmission is slowing the combine to prevent drum blockage. Raise the cutter or reduce width to relieve pressure.

text.name: rhm_tut_loss_msg
text.text: Grain loss behind the combine is critically high! Threshing rotor or cleaning shoe settings are misaligned. Open (Right Shift + K) to calibrate rotor speed, fan, and sieves.

text.name: rhm_tut_moisture_msg
text.text: Crop moisture is high or rain has begun! Wet straw and grain create immense internal friction, increasing engine load and harvest loss. Work during dry afternoon hours when possible.

text.name: rhm_tut_headland_msg
text.text: When lifting the cutter at headlands, the combine remembers your active harvesting speed. You will seamlessly re-enter rows without sudden braking.

text.name: rhm_tut_upgrade_msg
text.text: Basic combines require manual tuning. Upgrade electronics at the workshop to unlock Sensor Kits (Tier 2), Yield Monitors (Tier 3), or Opti-Harvest AI Autopilot (Tier 4).

text.name: rhm_tut_hud_drag_msg
text.text: You can reposition the HUD anywhere across your screen by holding Left Mouse Button (LMB) on the panel, or magnetically dock it cleanly beneath the F1 menu and screen edges.

text.name: rhm_tut_trip_msg
text.text: Press Shift+J to review your field yield summary, financial loss analysis, and fleet status. To quickly reset the counter for a new field, hold Shift+R for 1 second in the cab!

text.name: rhm_tut_chopper_msg
text.text: Chopping straw consumes an extra 15–20% of engine power compared to laying a swath. If you need more harvesting speed on dense crops, switch to laying a swath.

text.name: rhm_setting_wear_loss_long
text.text: Simulates grain loss from equipment wear. Dull header knives shatter crop heads (up to +3% loss and +15% power drag). A worn threshing drum and sieves drop unseparated grain (up to +3% loss).

text.name: rhm_tab_trip_desc
text.text: Live telemetry for harvested volume, worked area, average yield, and financial losses for the active field operation.

text.name: rhm_tab_analytics_desc
text.text: Loss distribution, operator efficiency ranking grade, and onboard diagnostic computer recommendations.

text.name: rhm_tab_fleet_desc
text.text: Real-time telemetry, throughput, and status of all harvesters on your farm.

text.name: rhm_tab_settings_desc
text.text: Configure hired worker cruise limiter, volunteer weed generation, and auto-reset options.

text.name: rhm_trip_footer_hint
text.text: Trip odometer tracks harvested area and clean grain volume for the active field. You can reset at any time.

text.name: rhm_rank_desc_a
text.text: Loss rate is below 1.5%. Combine setup and speed are perfectly balanced.

text.name: rhm_rank_desc_b
text.text: Loss rate between 1.5% and 3.0%. Consider minor speed or concave adjustments.

text.name: rhm_rank_desc_c
text.text: Loss rate between 3.0% and 4.5%. Reduce speed or inspect header sharpness.

text.name: rhm_rank_desc_d
text.text: Loss rate exceeds 4.5%! Severe sieve overloading or miscalibration detected.

text.name: rhm_advice_perfect
text.text: Harvesting efficiency is optimal. All separation parameters are well-balanced.

text.name: rhm_advice_speed
text.text: Dominant loss from excessive ground speed. Slow down to reduce sieve bed depth.

text.name: rhm_advice_moisture
text.text: Losses driven by high crop moisture or morning dew. Wait for field drying or reduce speed.

text.name: rhm_advice_wear
text.text: Elevated losses due to worn cutter knives or rasp bars. Service equipment at the workshop.

text.name: rhm_advice_slope
text.text: Lateral tilt on slopes causing uneven shoe loading. Reduce speed along side hills.

text.name: rhm_setting_ai_limiter_desc
text.text: Automatically caps cruise speed for hired workers when loss exceeds threshold.

text.name: rhm_setting_ai_threshold_desc
text.text: Maximum acceptable loss percentage before AI helper automatically brakes.

text.name: rhm_setting_volunteer_desc
text.text: Generates weed and volunteer sprouts behind combines in heavy loss zones (>3%).

text.name: rhm_setting_autoreset_desc
text.text: Automatically archive the current operation and reset the field counter when moving to a different field.

text.name: rhm_tab_fields_desc
text.text: Comprehensive field-level production, yields, losses, and contract operations for your farm.

text.name: rhm_loss_disabled_desc
text.text: Crop loss simulation is disabled in mod settings.

text.name: rhm_slopeloss_long
text.text: Simulates grain pooling on one side of cleaning shoe sieves on hillsides and slopes exceeding 4° (up to 5% loss). Turn off to eliminate terrain tilt penalties.

text.name: rhm_weedload_long
text.text: Juicy and fibrous weeds wrap around threshing cylinders and increase mechanical resistance and engine load (up to +25%). Turn off to prevent weeds from affecting engine power.
